provenance_note: The D1-D29 mapping, source-grounded summaries, categories, and item locators were checked against the published supplement. Public labels and operational fields are original adaptations; they are not quoted source headings or author-validated AI rules.
license_boundary: The Price et al. supplement is an attributed source, not bundled content. This registry does not reproduce the full decision definitions or a full translation.

field_provenance.source_grounded_note: source_definition_summary is an attributed concise paraphrase of the cited decision meaning; it does not validate any downstream AI behavior.
field_provenance.public_label_note: The schema field official_label stores an original public-facing noun phrase, not the source heading.

non_decision_themes.source_note: Supplementary Text p. 9 lists items 30–34 under Non-Decision Themes, not the 29 decisions.

decisions.source_definition_summary: Identifies consequential questions, emerging directions, and openings created by recent advances.
decisions.research_translation: Decide which research problem is worth attention before optimizing how to solve it.
trigger_signals: The request asks what to study next
Several plausible topics compete for attention
A new dataset, method, or result may change what is feasible
required_state: current evidence on gaps and trends
observable_good_behaviors: Names whose problem it is and what consequence would follow
Tests trend claims against primary or authoritative sources
common_failure_modes: Selects a topic before defining value criteria
Treats a single recent paper as a field consensus
confusable_with: D2 asks whether an opportunity fits the solver
D27 asks implications after results exist
evidence_needed: authoritative field agendas or primary literature
evidence that the claimed gap is current
possible_next_actions: record why one question matters now
revisit_conditions: a major field result closes or opens the gap
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No defensible field boundary or value criterion can be established
The task would require unauthorized strategic or sensitive information
do_not_infer: Do not infer importance from novelty alone
Do not infer a gap from absence in a small search
decisions.ai_ml_example: Choose whether robustness under distribution shift is a higher-value target than another benchmark gain, using deployment failures and unresolved mechanisms as evidence.
decisions.counterexample: The user already chose a fixed benchmark and only asks to format its results; agenda selection is not the current decision.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering
source_refs.locator: supplement PDF pp. 5–6, Supplementary Text, item 1

decisions.source_definition_summary: Assesses whether a real opportunity is especially accessible given the solver's capabilities, perspective, and resources.
decisions.research_translation: Match a research gap to the team’s comparative advantage without mistaking familiarity for value.
trigger_signals: A gap is plausible but ownership is unclear
Execution depends on rare data, skills, or access
The team is choosing among opportunities
observable_good_behaviors: Names capabilities and missing capabilities explicitly
Considers collaboration or acquisition instead of binary fit
common_failure_modes: Rejects unfamiliar work without considering partners
confusable_with: D1 concerns field importance
D9 concerns overall solvability and worth
evidence_needed: team skills and prior validated work
access to data, compute, participants, or facilities
possible_next_actions: select the opportunity with a defensible access advantage
revisit_conditions: a pilot exposes an unrecognized capability gap
a competing group removes the timing advantage
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Critical capability or legal access cannot be obtained
Fit cannot be assessed without disclosing protected information
do_not_infer: Do not infer fit from credentials alone
Do not claim exclusivity from lack of visible competitors
decisions.ai_ml_example: A lab with longitudinal clinical labels evaluates a calibration question that public benchmark teams cannot test, while documenting missing causal-inference expertise.
decisions.counterexample: Comparing two model architectures after the research question and team are fixed is not an expertise-opportunity decision.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Defines the goal, scope, requirements, constraints, and criteria by which a solution will be judged.
decisions.research_translation: Turn a broad research request into a bounded, testable decision contract.
trigger_signals: Permissions, time, or scope are undefined
confusable_with: D14 orders work after criteria exist
D28 tailors communication to an audience
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Required authority, ethics approval, or data rights are absent
No decision-relevant success criterion can be established
do_not_infer: Do not infer permission from technical access
Do not infer the true objective from a proxy metric
decisions.ai_ml_example: Define an ML study as improving patient-level AUROC without leakage, with subgroup calibration and a fixed compute budget as acceptance constraints.
decisions.counterexample: Choosing whether to use a transformer or a tree model is a candidate-solution question, not goal definition.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Selects the underlying features, concepts, relevant information, and useful representations for the problem.
decisions.research_translation: Decide what aspects of the system must be represented for reasoning to be valid.
trigger_signals: Available variables are numerous but relevance is unclear
observable_good_behaviors: Explains why each feature is relevant
Separates observed variables from latent concepts
Uses a representation suited to the causal or predictive question
common_failure_modes: Uses all available columns without rationale
Drops inconvenient variables before checking bias
confusable_with: D17 reorganizes evidence already collected
D5 chooses relationships and predictive structure
possible_next_actions: draw a system or causal map
select a minimal feature set with rationale
revisit_conditions: new evidence reveals an omitted mechanism
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Core constructs cannot be measured or represented well enough for the claim
Feature use would violate rights or introduce unmitigable harm
do_not_infer: Do not infer causal importance from model feature importance
Do not treat a convenient proxy as the construct itself
decisions.ai_ml_example: Represent repeated patient measurements with patient, visit, and record levels before designing a model split.
decisions.counterexample: Reformatting a completed results table for readability is D17 or D29, not problem framing.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Chooses or constructs a framework linking key features at the mechanism and structural level useful for prediction.
decisions.research_translation: Select the explanatory or predictive structure that generates discriminating expectations.
trigger_signals: Predictions are not derived from an explicit structure
Several mechanisms explain the same observation
The current framework is too coarse or too detailed
common_failure_modes: Names an algorithm without a scientific model
Fits a framework only because it predicts well in-sample
confusable_with: D8 selects candidate solutions or interventions
D23 revisits an existing framework after new evidence
possible_next_actions: choose a minimally sufficient mechanism level
revisit_conditions: new evidence violates a key prediction
an alternative framework explains anomalies better
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No framework yields testable or decision-relevant predictions
Framework selection would be pure post-hoc storytelling
do_not_infer: Do not equate predictive framework with software architecture
Do not infer mechanism from accuracy alone
decisions.ai_ml_example: Compare a shortcut-learning account with a robust-feature account and derive subgroup and perturbation predictions before training.
decisions.counterexample: Selecting among three deployment thresholds is choosing candidate solutions under D8 or D22, not a predictive framework.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Narrows a broad problem into specific questions and hypotheses that can be investigated.
decisions.research_translation: Choose the smallest research question whose answer would materially reduce uncertainty.
trigger_signals: The topic spans many causal paths or outcomes
No single experiment could answer the request
observable_good_behaviors: Produces a bounded unit of analysis and outcome
Preserves connection to the broader goal
common_failure_modes: Narrows to what is easy rather than informative
Creates a yes/no question with no discriminating test
Silently changes the population or outcome
confusable_with: D11 decomposes an already bounded problem
D13 identifies information required to distinguish options
possible_next_actions: fix population, intervention/exposure, comparator, and outcome where applicable
revisit_conditions: the narrowed question cannot distinguish alternatives
new evidence shifts the central uncertainty
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Any feasible narrowing would no longer answer the stated goal
The only available question is non-falsifiable
do_not_infer: Do not infer that narrower always means better
Do not discard important populations merely for convenience
decisions.ai_ml_example: Narrow ‘make language models safer’ to whether a specific intervention reduces refusal drift under a predefined adversarial distribution.
decisions.counterexample: Splitting model training, evaluation, and documentation into work packages is D11 decomposition.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Identifies prior problems or work whose solution process or result may transfer to the present context.
decisions.research_translation: Use literature and experience to find analogies while testing whether their assumptions transfer.
trigger_signals: A method is proposed by analogy
Novelty or baseline adequacy is uncertain
observable_good_behaviors: Separates surface similarity from structural similarity
Records what does and does not transfer
common_failure_modes: Copies a fashionable method without checking assumptions
Calls a problem novel after a shallow search
confusable_with: D1 assesses field importance
D24 asks whether new knowledge is needed after reflection
evidence_needed: comparable datasets, mechanisms, and evaluation settings
revisit_conditions: a new close analogue is found
stop_or_abstain_conditions: The needed literature cannot be lawfully accessed or verified
Transfer would rely on materially incompatible settings
do_not_infer: Do not infer novelty from search failure
Do not treat multiple pages for one work as independent sources
decisions.ai_ml_example: Compare prior domain-generalization studies by shift mechanism rather than merely reusing the most cited benchmark.
decisions.counterexample: Checking whether a newly collected result is reliable is D18, not related-work search.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Generates plausible candidate solutions consistent with the identified key features and criteria.
decisions.research_translation: Create competing interventions, models, explanations, or designs before committing to one.
trigger_signals: Only one solution is being considered
The current option fails a criterion
observable_good_behaviors: Includes a credible null or status-quo option
Links each option to expected outcomes
common_failure_modes: Produces cosmetic variants of one idea
confusable_with: D5 chooses the structure that makes predictions
D22 evaluates and refines candidates using accumulated evidence
possible_next_actions: add a null or simpler candidate
revisit_conditions: evidence supports a previously excluded class
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No candidate can meet hard safety or feasibility constraints
Candidate generation would facilitate disallowed harm
do_not_infer: Do not infer that more candidates imply better coverage
Do not treat a predictive framework as the solution itself
decisions.ai_ml_example: Compare data augmentation, invariant-risk training, and a no-intervention baseline as distinct responses to shortcut learning.
decisions.counterexample: Choosing a causal graph that explains shortcut formation is D5, even if it later informs an intervention.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Judges whether the problem is plausibly solvable and worth pursuing given difficulty, constraints, risk, and uncertainty.
decisions.research_translation: Make an explicit continue, pilot, pivot, or stop decision before costly execution.
trigger_signals: Risks or costs dominate the plausible gain
observable_good_behaviors: Uses a bounded pilot to resolve uncertainty
common_failure_modes: Declares impossible from one failed attempt
confusable_with: D2 assesses fit to a particular solver
D25 evaluates whether an ongoing approach is working
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Hard permission, safety, or physical feasibility gate fails
Expected learning cannot justify the cost or harm
do_not_infer: Do not infer impossibility from absence of a known method
Do not infer worth from feasibility alone
decisions.ai_ml_example: Before a full foundation-model run, test whether the signal survives on a smaller model and whether compute and data licenses permit scaling.
decisions.counterexample: Selecting which analysis to run on already collected data is D16.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Chooses simplifications that make the problem tractable and tests them against established criteria.
decisions.research_translation: Decide prospectively what detail may be omitted without invalidating the research decision.
trigger_signals: A proxy or subset is proposed
observable_good_behaviors: States each approximation and expected effect
Retains a route to increase fidelity
common_failure_modes: Uses convenience samples without scope limits
confusable_with: D23 re-evaluates earlier assumptions or simplifications after new evidence
D5 chooses the predictive structure
possible_next_actions: choose the least complex adequate representation
revisit_conditions: an anomaly appears near a simplification
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No tractable approximation preserves the decision-relevant property
Approximation error cannot be bounded
do_not_infer: Do not infer that a small pilot generalizes to full scale
Do not hide simplification in implementation detail
decisions.ai_ml_example: Use a smaller model for mechanism smoke tests only after defining which scaling-dependent claims it cannot support.
decisions.counterexample: After a failed full run, reconsidering whether the small-model proxy was valid is D23.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Breaks a problem into tractable pieces with their own sub-goals and interfaces.
decisions.research_translation: Choose a decomposition that permits independent progress without losing cross-part dependencies.
trigger_signals: No single action can resolve the problem
common_failure_modes: Confuses a task list with conceptual decomposition
Hides the hardest dependency between parts
confusable_with: D6 narrows the research question
D14 prioritizes among already defined tasks
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Decomposition would destroy the phenomenon being studied
Interfaces cannot be specified sufficiently
do_not_infer: Do not infer independence from organizational separation
Do not treat sequential steps as independent subproblems by default
decisions.ai_ml_example: Separate data leakage audit, baseline reproduction, intervention test, and subgroup evaluation while retaining one patient-level split contract.
decisions.counterexample: Selecting only one subgroup as the entire research scope is D6 narrowing, not decomposition.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Identifies the parts of a solving plan with the greatest difficulty or uncertainty and acceptable uncertainty at each stage.
decisions.research_translation: Locate the uncertainty bottleneck that most threatens valid progress.
observable_good_behaviors: Identifies the downstream consequence of each uncertainty
confusable_with: D14 chooses what to do first using multiple considerations
D24 reflects on whether knowledge is sufficient
revisit_conditions: an uncertainty is resolved or worsens
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Critical uncertainty cannot be reduced or bounded before irreversible action
The uncertainty estimate would be fabricated
do_not_infer: Do not infer low uncertainty from agreement among dependent sources
Do not convert ordinal judgments into unsupported probabilities
decisions.ai_ml_example: Identify whether label noise or distribution shift is the main threat before spending compute on architecture search.
decisions.counterexample: Choosing the next task because it is cheapest, with uncertainties already known, is D14 priority setting.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Specifies the information sufficient to solve the problem or distinguish candidate solutions.
decisions.research_translation: Define prospectively the evidence that would change the current research choice.
trigger_signals: A claim lacks a decisive observable
The next data request is vague
observable_good_behaviors: Connects each datum to a decision
common_failure_modes: Collects more data without a decision link
confusable_with: D24 is reflective and asks whether additional knowledge is needed after reviewing the current state
D15 specifies how to obtain already identified information
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No observable evidence can distinguish the alternatives
Required information cannot be collected ethically or lawfully
do_not_infer: Do not infer that more information is always useful
Do not route to D24 without explicit re-review of knowledge state
decisions.ai_ml_example: Before comparing two robustness mechanisms, specify which perturbation and subgroup outcomes would distinguish them.
decisions.counterexample: After surprising results reveal a missing domain fact, deciding whether to learn or recheck it is D24.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Chooses what to do first among competing considerations and how to allocate necessary resources.
decisions.research_translation: Order actions using blocking impact, uncertainty reduction, constraints, cost, and reversibility.
observable_good_behaviors: Keeps reversible probes ahead of irreversible commitments when informative
common_failure_modes: Prioritizes easy work over consequential uncertainty
confusable_with: D12 identifies uncertainty hotspots
D15 designs the information-acquisition plan
possible_next_actions: reserve up to two secondary actions
revisit_conditions: new evidence shifts expected information gain
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No authorized action can address the blocker
All actions are dominated by a safer or cheaper alternative
do_not_infer: Do not sum invented scores
Do not infer priority from recency or stakeholder volume alone
decisions.ai_ml_example: Reproduce the strongest baseline before running ablations because every later comparison depends on it.
decisions.counterexample: Determining that leakage is the dominant uncertainty is D12; ordering the leakage audit first is D14.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Designs and carries out a concrete information-gathering approach with milestones, metrics, and contingent paths.
decisions.research_translation: Convert an evidence need into an executable, branching research protocol.
trigger_signals: Needed evidence is known but acquisition is unspecified
Milestones or fallback paths are missing
A tool choice must match the evidence need
required_state: information requirement from D13 or D24
observable_good_behaviors: Specifies method, inputs, milestones, and decision rules
Keeps collection aligned to the needed evidence
common_failure_modes: Has no response to null or unexpected results
confusable_with: D13 defines what information is needed
D16 chooses calculations and analysis for obtained information
possible_next_actions: execute a bounded search or pilot
revisit_conditions: method fails to obtain valid information
stop_or_abstain_conditions: The acquisition method lacks permission or acceptable risk
No method can produce decision-relevant evidence
do_not_infer: Do not infer evidence quality from procedural completeness
Do not collect data before resolving leakage-critical choices
decisions.ai_ml_example: Freeze patient-level splits, baseline, seeds, metrics, and null-result branches before launching an ML experiment.
decisions.counterexample: Choosing which statistical model to apply after data collection is D16.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Chooses and performs calculations or analyses needed to interpret the available data.
decisions.research_translation: Select an analysis whose estimand, assumptions, and uncertainty match the research decision.
trigger_signals: Data exist but the decision-relevant estimate is missing
observable_good_behaviors: Defines the estimand before the method
Matches analysis to design and grouping
confusable_with: D17 concerns representation and organization
D21 determines justified conclusions
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Data provenance or design is too weak for the proposed analysis
Only outcome-driven analysis choices remain
do_not_infer: Do not infer causality from an unmatched analysis
Do not treat statistical significance as practical importance
decisions.ai_ml_example: Estimate patient-level performance with grouped bootstrap intervals rather than treating repeated visits as independent.
decisions.counterexample: Deciding how to visualize subgroup trade-offs is D17.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Chooses a representation and organization of evidence that creates clarity and reveals useful structure.
decisions.research_translation: Arrange collected information so comparisons, dependencies, and anomalies become inspectable.
trigger_signals: Important comparisons are hard to see
A technical representation may reveal structure
observable_good_behaviors: Uses a representation aligned with the predictive framework
Makes missing and conflicting evidence visible
common_failure_modes: Uses a visually persuasive but misleading chart
confusable_with: D4 selects important concepts while framing
D29 chooses final presentation for communication
D21 judges what conclusions the evidence supports
D22 selects among candidate solutions; organizing their evidence is only a supporting action
possible_next_actions: draw a dependency or causal diagram
revisit_conditions: new evidence adds a missing dimension
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Any available representation would expose restricted data
Aggregation would make the decision materially misleading
do_not_infer: Do not infer truth from visual coherence
Do not erase null or opposing evidence
Do not make D17 primary when representation is only a supporting step for an unresolved analysis, anomaly, conclusion, or selection decision
decisions.ai_ml_example: Organize model errors by subgroup, shift type, and seed with links to raw runs so an anomaly cluster becomes visible.
decisions.counterexample: Choosing which variables are conceptually part of the problem before collection is D4.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Evaluates whether information is valid, reliable, credible, and affected by bias.
decisions.research_translation: Audit source identity, provenance, measurement, leakage, dependence, and bias before using evidence.
trigger_signals: A key claim rests on uncertain evidence
Sources may be aliases or dependent
common_failure_modes: Accepts a landing page as verified full text
Trusts benchmark scores without split audit
confusable_with: D21 decides what conclusion follows after credibility is assessed
D20 investigates a particular deviation from expectation
revisit_conditions: a correction or alias is discovered
stop_or_abstain_conditions: A critical claim has no verifiable evidence
Evidence use would violate license, privacy, or authorization
do_not_infer: Do not infer credibility from prestige alone
Do not infer independent support from multiple URLs
Do not jump to a conclusion before D21
decisions.ai_ml_example: Detect that two reported robustness gains use the same underlying dataset and that one evaluation split leaks patient identity.
decisions.counterexample: After evidence is verified, deciding whether it supports a scoped claim is D21.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Compares new experimental or calculated information with expectations derived from the predictive framework.
decisions.research_translation: Test whether observed results match each competing framework’s preregistered predictions.
common_failure_modes: Compares only to a weak null
confusable_with: D20 decides whether and how to follow an anomaly
D23 revisits the framework or assumptions
possible_next_actions: trigger D20 or D23 when warranted
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No prior prediction can be reconstructed without hindsight
Observed data are not credible enough for comparison
do_not_infer: Do not infer framework truth from one match
Do not retrofit an expectation to the result
decisions.ai_ml_example: Compare subgroup calibration shifts to the directional predictions of two competing shortcut-learning mechanisms.
decisions.counterexample: Checking whether the subgroup labels themselves are reliable is D18.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Determines whether an unexpected result is meaningful and selects an appropriate follow-up.
decisions.research_translation: Triage deviations as expected variation, data or analysis defects, framework limits, or informative anomalies.
trigger_signals: A metric is implausibly strong or unstable
observable_good_behaviors: Plans discriminating follow-up rather than deleting it
common_failure_modes: Explains every anomaly with the preferred theory
confusable_with: D18 audits general evidence credibility
D19 performs the comparison that reveals a deviation
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Investigating would require unauthorized access or unsafe experimentation
The anomaly cannot be distinguished from measurement failure
do_not_infer: Do not infer novelty from surprise
Do not erase unexpected evidence without a trace
decisions.ai_ml_example: Investigate a single seed’s exceptional score by rerunning, checking split hashes, and testing whether a preprocessing cache leaked labels.
decisions.counterexample: A broad source-quality audit before any anomaly appears is D18.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Determines which conclusions are justified by the available data and their limitations.
decisions.research_translation: Calibrate each claim to the design, evidence strength, uncertainty, and scope.
trigger_signals: Results must be converted into claims
observable_good_behaviors: States supported, unsupported, and unresolved claims
Links every material claim to evidence
confusable_with: D18 asks whether evidence is believable
D27 explores broader implications beyond the immediate conclusion
possible_next_actions: reject or narrow an unsupported claim
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Critical evidence is invalid or missing
A conclusion would exceed what the design can identify
do_not_infer: Do not infer causality, generality, or safety beyond the evidence
Do not use credibility review as a substitute for claim calibration
decisions.ai_ml_example: Conclude that an intervention improved a fixed benchmark under specified shifts, while declining to claim real-world safety.
decisions.counterexample: Determining whether the benchmark result was leaked or independently reproduced is D18.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Evaluates and refines candidate solutions against all available information; more than one may remain.
decisions.research_translation: Select, reject, or refine candidates using explicit criteria and counterevidence.
trigger_signals: A decision must be made under residual uncertainty
observable_good_behaviors: Retains multiple options when evidence is tied
confusable_with: D8 generates candidates before evaluation
D26 actively tries to break the chosen solution
possible_next_actions: keep a Pareto set or reject all
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No candidate meets hard criteria
Comparisons are invalid or not commensurate
do_not_infer: Do not infer a single best solution when trade-offs remain
Do not select using test data tuning
decisions.ai_ml_example: Choose a simpler calibrated model over a marginally higher-AUROC model because it meets subgroup and deployment constraints.
decisions.counterexample: Listing plausible models before comparative evidence is D8.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Reconsiders whether earlier assumptions, simplifications, and predictive frameworks remain appropriate in light of new information.
decisions.research_translation: Reopen prior framing choices when evidence activates their revisit conditions.
trigger_signals: A simplification may explain an anomaly
observable_good_behaviors: Names which prior choice is reopened and why
Tests alternatives rather than patching ad hoc
common_failure_modes: Defends the original framework through exceptions
Confuses planned simplification with reflective revision
confusable_with: D10 chooses approximations prospectively
D5 selects a predictive framework initially
evidence_needed: new prediction mismatches or sensitivity results
stop_or_abstain_conditions: No test can distinguish revision from post-hoc accommodation
Changing assumptions would make the claim unfalsifiable
do_not_infer: Do not route here without new evidence or an activated revisit condition
Do not rewrite history; supersede it only after a replacement is accepted
Do not treat reopening or a temporary exception as automatic supersession
Do not use D23 as the default for an ordinary version change or operational hold that does not reopen an assumption or framework
decisions.ai_ml_example: After a scaling result reverses the small-model trend, reopen the assumption that mechanism behavior transfers across scale.
decisions.counterexample: Choosing the small-model approximation before any result is D10.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Reviews the solver’s current knowledge state to decide whether new information, learning, repetition, or cross-checking is needed.
decisions.research_translation: After reflecting on current evidence and competence, decide what must be learned or rechecked.
trigger_signals: Progress exposes a new concept gap
observable_good_behaviors: Names why prior information is insufficient
common_failure_modes: Routes every search request to reflection
Masks a capability gap as data scarcity
confusable_with: D13 prospectively specifies information needed to distinguish alternatives
D2 assesses broader solver–opportunity fit
possible_next_actions: return to D13 if a new evidence requirement is formed
stop_or_abstain_conditions: Required knowledge cannot be obtained or verified within constraints
Further searching has no decision link
do_not_infer: Do not infer D24 from ordinary information gathering; require explicit re-review
Do not count repeated access to the same source as new knowledge
decisions.ai_ml_example: After an unexplained calibration failure, recognize a missing understanding of prevalence shift and consult an independent methodological source.
decisions.counterexample: Before any run, defining which labels are needed to distinguish two hypotheses is D13.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Evaluates progress and decides whether the overall strategy or even the goals should change.
decisions.research_translation: Use milestones and learning rate to continue, modify, pivot, or stop the research approach.
trigger_signals: All live alternatives or proposed actions yield the same decision-relevant signal
The goal may no longer be appropriate
observable_good_behaviors: Preserves the failed or negative path when an honest post-hoc question or claim pivot is proposed
common_failure_modes: Continues because work has already been invested
Changes tactics without diagnosing the bottleneck
confusable_with: D9 is initial or renewed solvability/worth assessment
D26 evaluates the solution rather than the strategy
stop_or_abstain_conditions: The approach cannot reach the goal within constraints
Continuing would violate a stop condition
do_not_infer: Do not infer approach quality from effort or volume
Do not delete dead ends from the trace
decisions.ai_ml_example: Pivot from architecture search to data audit after three controlled runs show no stable gain and error analysis points to label drift.
decisions.counterexample: Testing whether the selected final model fails under adversarial perturbation is D26.

source_refs.citation: Price et al. (2021), A Detailed Characterization of the Expert Problem-Solving Process in Science and Engineering

decisions.source_definition_summary: Assesses the adequacy of a candidate or selected solution by probing failure modes, discipline-specific checks, and goal coverage.
decisions.research_translation: Try to break the solution before accepting it, and state its limits.
trigger_signals: Known failure modes have not been tested
confusable_with: D22 selects among candidates
D25 evaluates the research strategy
possible_next_actions: reject or provisionally accept the solution
stop_or_abstain_conditions: A critical failure mode is untested or fails
Testing would impose unacceptable harm
